metadata.content:
KoreLumina Handoff — Knowledge Operations Backend Activation
Mission Continuation — Complete the First Governed Knowledge Lifecycle Before Chief Agent Activation
You are continuing KoreLumina as the Lead Systems Architect and Principal Engineer.
This is not an MVP.
The immediate objective is to finish activating Knowledge Operations as KoreLumina’s governed knowledge factory, because this is the educational substrate from which the Chief Agent will eventually learn.
The Chief Agent must ultimately be able to learn from Genesis forward, which is why Knowledge Operations, education, governance, lineage, canonicalization, and Organizational Memory must be operational before Chief Agent runtime activation.
Do not continue building the Chief Agent production UI during this task.

Repository
Repository:
kore20lllc-netizen/korelumina
Branch:
inspect/runtime-certified-main
Before modifying anything:
Bashgit branch --show-current
git log -1 --oneline
git status --short
Inspect the current pushed HEAD before modification.
Preserve all local unstaged work unless explicitly part of the active ticket.
Do not stage or overwrite unrelated:
runtime-data/
runtime/knowledge/
local RuntimeHeader work
archived documentation work
evidence-admission work
other generated knowledge data
Generated runtime knowledge state is local operational data unless architecture explicitly requires otherwise.

Core Mission
Knowledge Operations must support a real governed lifecycle:
Source
→ Evidence
→ Knowledge IR
→ Validation
→ Knowledge Package
→ Canonical Review
→ Canonical Knowledge
→ Organizational Memory
The purpose is not merely storage.
Knowledge Operations is the knowledge manufacturing, governance, preservation, and educational system that prepares trustworthy knowledge for later Chief Agent learning.
The eventual Chief Agent path is:
Genesis
→ governed educational sources
→ Knowledge Operations
→ Canonical Knowledge
→ Organizational Memory
→ Chief Agent educational state
→ controlled learning
Do not bypass any governance layer for convenience.

Constitutional Authorities
Continue respecting all existing repository authorities, including:


Knowledge Constitution


Learning Constitution


Knowledge Package amendment


Canonical Knowledge amendment


Organizational Memory stewardship


Canonical → Organizational Memory adaptation contract


Chief Agent Operational Learning Model


Knowledge Operations certified UI contract


Do not redesign these contracts.
Reconcile implementations to them.

Non-Negotiable UI Rule
The Knowledge Operations UI was already visually certified before backend activation.
Therefore:


do not redesign Knowledge Operations;


do not replace the Knowledge Capsule Flow Engine;


do not alter the pill-capsule metaphor;


do not alter peeling/remediation/resealing semantics;


do not alter Executive Hero / Executive Ribbon composition;


do not introduce new layout ownership unnecessarily;


do not replace Lumina primitives;


do not change lifecycle visualization semantics without explicit visual approval.


Backend state must conform to the UI contract.
Where new operational controls are necessary, place them inside the existing certified composition.

Working Method
One responsibility at a time.
For every milestone:
Inspect
→ determine actual root cause / existing implementation
→ implement one responsibility
→ git diff --check
→ focused tests
→ npm run build
→ manual visual validation when UI changes
→ wait for user "green"
→ certify UI contract if applicable
→ commit
→ push
→ continue
Do not combine unrelated milestones.
Do not commit a UI change before visual approval.
Terminal-only edits.
Never ask the user to manually edit files.
Use complete automated patches or:
Bashcat > file <<'EOF'
...
EOF

Original Activation Acceptance Boundary
This tranche is complete only when all of the following are true:


automatic canonical promotion is impossible;


persistent Knowledge Packages exist;


governed Documentation Compiler exists;


real validation drives capsule integrity;


human Canonical Review is real;


only approved packages become Canonical Knowledge;


Canonical Knowledge projects into Organizational Memory;


Knowledge Operations displays those real states;


one real KoreLumina document completes the entire visible lifecycle;


full repository build is green;


architecture remains clean.


Then stop before Chief Agent consumption.

Original Milestone Sequence
The governing sequence remains:
1. Canonical Governance Boundary
2. Persistent Knowledge Package Boundary
3. Governed Documentation Compiler
4. Real Canonical Review
5. Canonical Promotion
6. Organizational Memory Projection
7. Knowledge Operations Real-State Wiring
8. First End-to-End Production Knowledge Capsule
9. Conversation Compiler
10. Knowledge Graph / Distribution follow-through
Do not jump ahead.
A large portion of 1–4 already existed and was audited/reconciled rather than rebuilt.

Current State — Completed / Proven
1. Automatic Canonical Promotion Boundary
Governance has been reinforced so:
Evidence
≠ Knowledge IR
≠ Validated Knowledge IR
≠ Knowledge Package
≠ Canonical Knowledge
Confidence is evidence of quality.
Confidence is not approval authority.
Canonical promotion remains separate from validation and Canonical Review.

2. Knowledge Package Lifecycle
Persistent Knowledge Packages exist and are being projected into the certified Knowledge Capsule UI.
Package identity was corrected to the compact six-digit convention.
Persistent lifecycle semantics are in place for the real slice.
Historical duplicate/useless capsule behavior was also cleaned up so old redundant capsules do not pollute the production UI.
Do not regress package identity or lifecycle presentation.

3. Documentation / Genesis Path
The first real documentation pipeline has already been substantially activated.
The original goal remains:
real approved repository document
→ Evidence
→ governed IR
→ validation
→ persisted Knowledge Package
→ awaiting_review
Do not create a parallel Documentation architecture.
Continue using existing compiler registry / normalization / validation infrastructure.

4. Canonical Review — Major Progress
Canonical Review has evolved from read-only projection into a governance command center inside the existing V3 Production composition.
The primary scalable queue modes now are:
All
Individual
Batch
Policy
Blocked
This was specifically required because reviewing thousands of capsules one-by-one is not operationally viable.
The Flow Engine remains lifecycle visualization.
Canonical Review is the human governance workspace.

Individual Review
Individual review has real backend support.
The UI supports explicit human decisions:
Approve
Require remediation
Reject
The decision does not automatically create Canonical Knowledge.
Human review remains separate from canonical promotion.

Batch Review
Batch governance exists.
Eligible packages can be grouped into a governed batch.
Batch compatibility was hardened so packages must share governance-compatible attributes such as authority and scope.
A batch human decision is applied while preserving package-level auditability.
Conceptual invariant:
Batch decision
→ batch lineage
→ individual package review records

NOT:

batch object replaces package governance history
Batch review UI is integrated into Canonical Review.

Policy Review Architecture — Current Major Workstream
Policy Governance has been substantially implemented.
A package may not self-authorize policy review merely by carrying metadata.
Current invariant:
package metadata says policy X
        ↓
exact policy ID + version
        ↓
separately persisted policy authority exists?
        ↓
active?
        ↓
human authorized?
        ↓
authority compatible?
        ↓
scope compatible?
        ↓
policy_candidate
Still:
policy_candidate ≠ approved
policy_candidate ≠ canonical

Persistent Policy Authority Store
Implemented under the Canonical Review governance domain.
Policy statuses:
draft
active
revoked
superseded
Policy records preserve at least:
id
version
status
title
authority
scope
owner
authorizedBy
authorizedAt
createdAt
updatedAt
supersedes[]
supersededBy
rules
Rules currently include governance requirements such as:
requireCompleteGovernanceIdentity
requireProvenance
requireValidationPassed
excludedAuthorities[]
A policy cannot become a policy authority just because package metadata claims it exists.

Policy Administration Lifecycle
Backend administration service supports:
createDraft()
activate()
revoke()
supersede()
Current intended lifecycle:
create
→ draft

draft
→ explicit human activation
→ active

active
→ revoke

active
→ supersede
→ old version = superseded
→ new version = active
Creation cannot directly produce an active policy.

Policy Runtime APIs
Runtime administration boundaries exist for:
POST /api/knowledge/canonical-review/policies
POST /api/knowledge/canonical-review/policies/:policyId/:version/activate
POST /api/knowledge/canonical-review/policies/:policyId/:version/revoke
POST /api/knowledge/canonical-review/policies/:policyId/:version/supersede
Read boundary:
GET /api/knowledge/canonical-review/policies
Governance responses explicitly preserve:
packageDecision: null
promotion: null
Policy administration itself does not approve packages and does not create Canonical Knowledge.

Builder Policy API
Builder has typed client support for:
getCanonicalReviewPolicies()
createCanonicalReviewPolicyDraft()
activateCanonicalReviewPolicy()
revokeCanonicalReviewPolicy()
supersedeCanonicalReviewPolicy()

Policy Administration UI
Inside:
Knowledge Operations
→ Production
→ Canonical Review
→ Policy
the existing certified composition now supports:
Create draft policy
Draft fields include:
Policy ID
Version
Owner
Policy title
Authority
Scope
Governance identity requirement
Provenance requirement
Validation requirement
Excluded authorities
A successful draft becomes a persisted Policy card.

Important UI Defects Already Solved
Do not regress these.
Input interaction
Policy Administration controls initially rendered but were not reliably clickable.
The interaction layer was repaired locally in Canonical Review.
Do not modify shared Lumina primitives for this.

Invisible input text
Browser/global styling was overriding inputs with a white surface while text remained light.
Policy form inputs now explicitly own:
dark background
light readable text
visible caret
visible placeholder
The same correction was applied to the Authorizing human input.
Do not remove those local overrides until the underlying global input styling is deliberately audited.

Policy Registry Refresh Defect
A successful POST initially persisted policies but the card did not appear.
Several related issues were found:
Refresh coupling
Canonical Review used a coupled refresh:
Promise.all([
  getCanonicalReviewSnapshot(),
  getCanonicalReviewPolicies(),
])
If either source failed, both visible state updates were lost.
This was changed toward independent refresh behavior.
Mutation/read race
A successful policy mutation was immediately followed by a refetch that could overwrite the successful local mutation before React painted it.
Current approach:
POST succeeds
→ use returned persisted policy
→ update Policy snapshot immediately
→ normal polling reconciles afterward
Do not restore synchronous post-mutation refetch behavior that can erase a successful policy card.

Policy Registry Scalability
The user explicitly identified that 10+ policies must not stretch and deform Canonical Review.
The persisted policy collection now has its own bounded vertical scroll viewport.
Current form:
max-h-[720px]
overflow-y-auto
overscroll-contain
scrollbar-gutter:stable
Conceptual layout:
Policy
├── Policy Summary
├── Policy Administration
│   └── Create Draft editor
│
└── Persisted Policy Registry
    ┌─────────────────────────────┐
    │ policy                       │
    │ policy                       │
    │ policy                       │
    │ policy                       │
    │ ...                          │
    │             ↕ scroll         │
    └─────────────────────────────┘
Do not make the entire Canonical Review panel scroll just to accommodate policy records.
Only the persisted registry owns this bounded scroll.

Human Policy Activation — Proven
A real draft policy was successfully activated.
Human identity used:
human:knowledge-governance
Activation persisted:
status = active
authorizedBy
authorizedAt
The UI transition was proven:
DRAFT
→ Human authorization required
→ Activate policy
→ ACTIVE
→ Authorized by <human> · <timestamp>

Human Policy Revocation — Proven
Real revocation was also executed successfully.
Latest observed local runtime policy state:
Policy@1.0.1
status: revoked
authorizedBy: human:knowledge-governance
authority: Owner
scope: platform
supersededBy: null
and:
Policy-Doc-Low-Risk@1.0.0
status: draft
authorizedBy: ""
authorizedAt: 0
authority: owner
scope: platform
Latest runtime summary:
total: 2
active: 0
draft: 1
revoked: 1
superseded: 0
These records are local runtime knowledge data.
Do not commit:
runtime/knowledge/review-policies/
unless architecture explicitly changes that rule.

Policy Revocation UI
Active policies now expose:
Revoke policy
then a two-step confirmation:
Revoke active policy

Revoking human
[ human:knowledge-governance ]

[ Confirm revocation ]
[ Cancel ]
Revocation means:
active
→ revoked
It does not:
delete policy history
undo historical package decisions
mutate Canonical Knowledge

CURRENT NEXT TICKET — Governed Draft Policy Deletion
This is the immediate next milestone.
The user explicitly requested the ability to delete policies that are no longer needed.
Do not implement unrestricted deletion.
Governance rule:
DRAFT
→ permanent deletion may be allowed
→ only if never activated
→ only if not referenced
→ only if not part of supersession lineage

ACTIVE
→ cannot delete
→ revoke first

REVOKED
→ cannot hard delete
→ retain as governance history

SUPERSEDED
→ cannot hard delete
→ retain as lineage history
The current unused draft:
Policy-Doc-Low-Risk@1.0.0
is the appropriate local test candidate after the feature is complete.

Draft Deletion — Required Backend
Add a governed deletion method to Policy Administration.
Suggested semantics:
TypeScriptdeleteDraft(
  policyId,
  version,
  decision
)
Required checks:
policy exists
status === draft
authorizedBy is empty
authorizedAt === 0
supersedes.length === 0
supersededBy === null
no package references policyId@version
If any check fails:
reject deletion
Do not silently downgrade or archive an active historical policy.
Permanent deletion is only for never-authorized, unused drafts.

Package Reference Check
Before deleting a draft, inspect actual Knowledge Package metadata/persistence.
A policy must not be deleted if any package references:
canonicalReviewPolicy.policyId
canonicalReviewPolicy.policyVersion
Do not fake this check.
Reuse the actual Knowledge Package store/service.
If no direct query exists, add the narrowest read helper necessary.

Draft Deletion Runtime API
Add something equivalent to:
DELETE
/api/knowledge/canonical-review/policies/:policyId/:version
Require human identity.
Response must explicitly preserve:
packageDecision: null
promotion: null
Suggested result:
JSON{
  "ok": true,
  "deleted": {
    "id": "...",
    "version": "..."
  },
  "packageDecision": null,
  "promotion": null
}
Do not expose filesystem paths.

Draft Deletion Builder Client
Add:
TypeScriptdeleteCanonicalReviewPolicyDraft(
  policyId,
  version,
  {
    actorId
  }
)
No UI until runtime tests/build are green.

Draft Deletion UI
Only draft policy cards may show:
Delete policy
Two-step confirmation:
Delete draft policy

This permanently removes:
Policy-Doc-Low-Risk@1.0.0

Only unused, never-authorized drafts can be deleted.

Deleting human
[ human:knowledge-governance ]

[ Permanently delete ]
[ Cancel ]
After successful deletion:
POST/DELETE response confirms persistence change
→ immediately remove policy from local registry
→ background poll reconciles
Do not wait exclusively for GET before updating the UI.
Do not allow deletion for:
active
revoked
superseded

Draft Deletion Focused Tests
Add at minimum:
draft with no references can be deleted
active policy cannot be deleted
revoked policy cannot be deleted
superseded policy cannot be deleted
authorized policy cannot be deleted
policy with Knowledge Package reference cannot be deleted
deleting one version does not delete another version
deletion cannot approve a package
deletion cannot promote canonical knowledge
Then:
Bashgit diff --check
focused tests
npm --workspace apps/lumina-runtime run build
npm --workspace apps/lumina-builder run build
Visual validation required before certification/commit.

AFTER DRAFT DELETION — Policy Supersession
Once draft deletion is green, implement Policy Supersession UI.
Backend supersession already exists.
Do not redesign it.
Required UX on an active policy:
Supersede policy
Open a new version form prefilled from the active policy.
Editable fields should include at least:
new version
title
authority
scope
owner
rules
excluded authorities
Do not mutate the existing active version.
Required transition:
Policy@1.0.1 active

Supersede
       ↓

Policy@1.0.1
status = superseded
supersededBy = Policy@2.0.0

Policy@2.0.0
status = active
supersedes = [Policy@1.0.1]
authorizedBy = human
authorizedAt = timestamp
Human identity required.
Verify UI and persisted lineage.

Policy History UI
Once supersession works, the registry should truthfully distinguish:
DRAFT
ACTIVE
REVOKED
SUPERSEDED
For superseded policy cards display:
Superseded by Policy@2.0.0
For replacement:
Supersedes Policy@1.0.1
Do not delete historical records.

AFTER POLICY ADMINISTRATION — Governed Policy Execution
Only after:
create draft
activate
revoke
supersede
delete unused draft
are all complete should policy execution be activated.
This is separate from policy administration.
Policy execution means applying an already-authorized policy to eligible Knowledge Packages.
It still must not directly bypass Canonical Promotion.

Policy Execution Required Flow
Conceptually:
active policy
        ↓
eligible package set
        ↓
evaluate every policy rule
        ↓
exceptions removed
        ↓
human executes governed policy
        ↓
review decision recorded per package
        ↓
package approvalState changes appropriately
        ↓
NO canonical promotion yet
Do not interpret:
policy exists
as:
package approved

Policy Execution UI
Inside:
Canonical Review
→ Policy
an ACTIVE policy should eventually show:
Eligible packages       N
Compliant packages      N
Exceptions              N
Blocked                 N

[ Inspect eligible set ]
[ Review exceptions ]
[ Execute governed policy ]
Execution requires human confirmation.
Audit must preserve:
policy ID
policy version
executing human
execution timestamp
package IDs
rule evaluation
exceptions
decision generated for each package

POLICY EXECUTION TESTS
At minimum:
draft policy cannot execute
revoked policy cannot execute
superseded policy cannot execute
active policy may execute
authority mismatch excluded
scope mismatch excluded
failed validation excluded
excluded authority cannot execute
package receives explicit review decision
package remains non-canonical after policy approval
execution history persists
policy version is immutable in execution history

THEN RETURN TO ORIGINAL MILESTONE 5 — Canonical Promotion
Once Individual / Batch / Policy Canonical Review paths are all real and governed, continue the original handoff.
Canonical promotion must only accept an explicitly approved Knowledge Package/review decision.
Required preservation:
provenance
Knowledge Package ID
review/approval evidence
authority
scope
version
lineage
lifecycle history
Canonical promotion must not mutate/delete the source package.
Existing canonical read/query APIs must continue working.
Required tests:
pending review cannot promote
rejected review cannot promote
remediation_required cannot promote
revoked policy does not retroactively destroy valid prior review history
explicit approved review may promote
canonical record retains package reference
canonical record retains provenance
alternate KPP/platform preservation path cannot bypass review
Commit separately.

Milestone 6 — Canonical → Organizational Memory Projection
Implement / verify the constitutional adaptation path:
Canonical Knowledge
→ governed adaptation
→ Organizational Memory
Organizational Memory is the steward, not canonical authority.
Preserve:
canonical source reference
package reference / lineage
source provenance
scope
privacy classification
approval state
supersession state
consumer-visible trust
Only constitutionally permitted adaptations:
summarization
indexing
generalized projection
retrieval optimization
privacy-safe adaptation
Do not transfer canonical ownership to memory.

Milestone 7 — Knowledge Operations Real-State Wiring
Replace fixture state only where real backend state exists.
Keep the complete Flow Engine visible.
Real lifecycle slice must visibly support:
Documentation source
→ IR
→ Validation

source
provenance
compiler history
IR
validation history
review state
canonical state
memory projection
timeline
destination
Metrics must be truthful.
If a metric is not backed by real infrastructure:
unavailable
partial
not invented.

Milestone 8 — First Real End-to-End Production Knowledge Capsule
Use one real approved KoreLumina document.
Do not fabricate content.
Choose something:
approved
authoritative enough to teach
stable
traceable
safe
Required proof:
real repository document

capsule ID
source

Chief Agent Boundary
Do not continue Chief Agent operational/runtime wiring in this tranche.
The current Chief Agent workspace remains a read-model/prototype boundary until Knowledge Operations is fully operational.

That chain is the reason Knowledge Operations exists.
